notes: Step 1 change: dropped the speaker-8ohm node. The tutorial's 'speakers or headphones' plug into the Pi's audio jack, not the GPIO circuit. The catalogue's Pi GPIO type has no audio port, and a bare 8-ohm speaker is not what the tutorial describes. So it would be an unconnected node.
GPIO numbers map to 40-pin header pins as follows: GPIO4 = pin 7, GPIO17 = pin 11, GPIO27 = pin 13, GPIO10 = pin 19. Ground is header pin 6. These are the pin numbers in the tutorial's code.
Each button is wired between its GPIO pin and ground. gpiozero's Button uses the Pi's internal pull-up, so no external resistor is needed.

Each button straddles the centre gap, with side 1 (1.l, 1.r) on the top half and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) on the bottom half. The GPIO lead goes into the same column strip as side 1, and a pin-to-pin jumper takes side 2 to the ground rail bn.

The five pin-to-socket leads are 4 button signal leads plus 1 ground lead. For these leads, end a is the male pin into the breadboard and end b is the female socket on the Pi header pin. The four pin-to-pin jumpers link each button's side 2 to the ground rail.
The tutorial lets you choose any GPIO pins, so the exact breadboard columns and the wire-to-rail positions are assumptions. The GPIO numbers come from the example code.
